title: Charge each payment once, however often the shop calls

blocks.text: The gateway's `POST /payments` now keeps its idempotency keys in a database table instead of a map in memory, so that they survive a restart and every gateway node sees the same keys. Shops' HTTP clients give up after a few seconds and call again with the same `Idempotency-Key`. Some call twice at once from two servers, and one shop's release reused keys for a day.

Write `pay` in `src/main/java/com/example/practice/PaymentsEndpoint.java`. A cardholder pays at most once for each payment a shop sends, and every call, first or repeated, tells the shop the truth about that payment with one of the statuses listed on `Result`.

Everything else is in the file. `KeyTable` behaves like a table with a unique constraint on its key column. `Host.request` returns `null` when no answer came in time. `purchase` builds the 0200, `reversalOf` the 0420 that undoes it (add it to `reversals`, which a store-and-forward sender delivers), and `outcomeOf` reads the host's answer. About twenty lines.

cases.says: a first call sends one 0200 and tells the shop the host's approval
a retry with the same key gets the first call's answer and sends nothing
when the host never answered, the purchase is reversed once and a retry with the key is told it failed, without a second 0200
a key sent again with another payment is refused instead of answered with the first payment's approval
a retry that arrives while the first call still waits for the host is told so and sends nothing
two identical payments with their own keys are two purchases

origin.section: 12.5. A Retried Call Carries the Same Idempotency Key, So It Is Applied Once

concepts: The gateway claims each idempotency key atomically, refuses it for another payment and answers every retry with the stored outcome, failures included, so one key sends at most one 0200.
